Only methods declared in sugar-log/src, or inherited from a parent declared there, are listed. A type that extends a class outside that tree, such as \RuntimeException, does not show the methods of that class.

static removePanicHandler(): voidUninstall the handler registered by self::installPanicHandler(), restoring the exception handling that existed before the FIRST install (PHP's builtin default when there was none). PHP cannot unregister the companion shutdown hook, so the install epoch is advanced and every registered hook self-retires. Idempotent: with nothing installed this is a no-op — it never pops a handler sugar-log does not own. self::reset() deliberately does NOT uninstall the panic handler; this method is its counterpart (install is process-lifetime state like setOutput, and must be undoable without one).
static restoreTerminal(bool $force = false): voidRestore the terminal to a usable state: exit altscreen and show cursor.

Which LogRecords to keep: LogFilter::new()->withMinLevel(Level::Warn) ->withField('svc', 'api')->apply($records).

MethodSummary
static new(): selfA filter that keeps every record.
withMinLevel(?Level $level): selfKeep records at $level or above; null drops the condition. A record whose level could not be read is not known to meet a threshold, so it is dropped while one is set.

One beat of a LogViewer's follow chain: the LogViewer::tick() timer fired. It carries no records; the viewer decides on taking it whether to read, so the read always uses the viewer's current reader and follow setting instead of the ones the timer was armed with.

LogViewer final class

A TEA log viewer: the newest records of a log file, through a LogFilter, following the file as it grows.

Not listed: the methods of SugarCraft\Core\Concerns\Mutable, a trait declared outside src/.

MethodSummary
static new(LogReader $reader, ?LogFilter $filter = null): selfA following viewer over $reader. With no $filter every record shows. Nothing is read until the Cmd from init() runs.
init(): ?\ClosureThe first read, whether or not the viewer follows (a viewer that never read has nothing to show), which also starts the follow chain.
update(Msg $msg): array
view(): stringThe filtered records that fit, one row each, exactly $height rows. Blank rows fill the space the records leave, after them: a view holding fewer records than its height shows them from the top row, so the newest sits on the bottom row only once the records fill the view.
subscriptions(): ?Subscriptions
refresh(): \ClosureA Cmd that reads the tail now and hands it back as a LogTailMsg, without waiting for the next tick: after withReader() or withFollow() it catches up at once instead of an interval later. It is a one-off read and never starts a second follow chain.
tick(): \ClosureA Cmd that hands back a LogTickMsg after $interval seconds: one beat of the follow chain init() starts. The viewer decides on taking the tick whether to read, so nothing is read here. The chain reschedules itself; issuing this yourself starts a second one.
visibleRecords(): arrayThe held records the filter keeps, oldest first — every record the viewer could show, before the height cut.
withReader(LogReader $reader): selfRead another file. Reads of the old one in flight are dropped; a following viewer's chain reads the new one at its next tick, or issue refresh() to read it at once. A paused viewer reads nothing on a tick, so it keeps showing the old file's records until it resumes or a refresh() reads the new one.
withFilter(LogFilter $filter): self
withFollow(bool $follow): selfFollow the file or freeze on what is held. A change drops the reads in flight, so a paused viewer takes no late read. The follow chain keeps running while paused without reading, so a resumed viewer reads again at the next tick; issue refresh() to read at once (the f key does). Setting the current value changes nothing.
withInterval(float $seconds): self
withTailSize(int $records): selfHow many records each read takes from the end of the file. A strict filter shows only the matches among them, so size it for the filter. Each read replaces what is held, so when more than $records lines arrive between two reads (a burst, or a pause) only the newest $records are ever shown and the rest are skipped without a mark; size it above the lines one interval can bring.
withHeight(int $rows): self
withWidth(?int $columns): selfPad and clip every row to $columns cells; null renders rows at their own width. A clipped row ends in ….
withShowTimestamps(bool $show): selfShow a structured record's time as [time]. A text line shows as written either way.
withShowLevel(bool $show): selfShow a structured record's level as [INF]. A text line shows as written either way.
withScrollToBottom(bool $bottom): selfShow the newest records (true) or the oldest of those held (false) when they overflow the height.
withColor(bool $color): selfColor each row by its level; false renders plain text.
withStyles(Styles $styles): selfTake the level palette from $styles. The styles are read once here, so editing $styles afterwards does not reach this viewer.

PsrBridge final class

PSR-3 bridge wrapping a Logger instance.

MethodSummary
__construct(Logger $logger, ?HookRegistry $hooks = null)
emergency(string|\Stringable $message, array $context = []): void
alert(string|\Stringable $message, array $context = []): void
critical(string|\Stringable $message, array $context = []): void

log(mixed $level, string|\Stringable $message, array $context = []): voidPSR-3 generic entry. The interface leaves $level untyped; only the eight PSR-3 level strings (as string or Stringable) resolve. Anything else — an unknown string, a number, null, an array — is a caller error and raises InvalidArgumentException as PSR-3 sanctions, instead of silently mislabeling the record as Info.
